events.objective: Determine whether the reported payment failures are real and when they started. Around 2026-04-02T12:17-12:32Z, look beyond HTTP error-rate: check payment-service request rate, latency, business-level failure signals (declined/failed transfer counts, status fields in logs, 200-with-error-body patterns), logs for error signatures mentioning bank/acquirer/transfer/decline/timeout, and any affected dependency traces. Report onset time, exact error signatures, and which services/endpoints actually show anomalies vs. the green error-rate panel.

Identify what changed across ALL services (not just payment-service) in the window 2026-04-02T10:00Z-13:00Z: list deployments and config changes, especially to payment-service's dependencies (bank/acquirer gateway, transfer/ledger workers, queues, shared infrastructure). Also map payment-service's dependency graph and shared components, and search historical incidents for the same 'users report failures but error rate green' pattern with its known root cause.

Correlate the changes found in task b against the symptom onset found in task a. For each candidate change (deploy/config) in the onset window, check whether the downstream dependency it touched shows a matching resource/error/latency trend in the same minutes. Conclude which specific change, if any, is the most likely trigger and whether the failure is in payment-service itself or a downstream dependency.

args.query: users report payment failures but error rate green

events.statement: payment-service ERROR logs begin at 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z with 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' and continue through 13:58:39Z (311 ERROR matches, 140 PENDING_RETRY + 171 cert-error). Onset is ~12:15-12:16Z.

The exact error signature is a TLS client-certificate expiry: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' — first_seen 2026-04-02T12:16:44Z, 171 occurrences.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate jumps from a flat 0.20% baseline through 12:08Z to 83.37% avg (max 100) in the 12:14Z bucket and 100.0% for every bucket from 12:20Z onward.
payment-service payment_success_rate collapses from ~99.04-99.81% (11:50-12:08Z) to 18.65% avg in the 12:14Z bucket, then ~2.4-2.7% for all buckets from 12:20Z through 13:56Z.

The HTTP error_rate panel is genuinely flat: error_rate stays in 0.16-0.26% across the whole 11:50-13:56Z window (min 0.1, max 0.32, mean 0.22), while request_rate (~100 req/s) is also unchanged and latency_p99_ms actually DROPS from ~317-330ms to ~139ms at 12:14Z onward.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no logs/metrics of its own; it must be observed through payment-service, its only caller.

payment-service does not emit an HTTP error for these failures (error_rate stays ~0.2%) while business-level bank_api_error_rate hits 100% — so the green error-rate panel does not reflect real payment outcomes; the failures are business-level/functional, not HTTP 5xx.

events.description: Could not confirm whether api-gateway or other upstream services show anomalies: api-gateway WARN/ERROR query for 12:00-13:59Z returned 0 matches (total_matched 0), so no evidence either way from this query.
bank-partner-api has no logs/metrics in the platform (external dependency), so its own side of the mTLS failure could not be inspected directly.

Within the 12:14Z 6-minute bucket, bank_api_error_rate already averaged 83.37% with max 100 and payment_success_rate 18.65% avg, but bucket granularity (360s) prevents pinning the exact second of transition between 12:14:00 and 12:20:00Z; the log-based onset (12:15:27Z) is the tightest bound obtained.

events.answer: The payment failures are real and start at ~2026-04-02T12:15Z. The HTTP error-rate panel is green by design flaw: the failures never reach an HTTP 5xx because payment-service returns a success-style response while marking transfers PENDING_RETRY after the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api is rejected. The exact signature is an expired client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, "tls: expired certificate (alert 45)"), with bank_api_error_rate jumping from 0.2% to 100% and payment_success_rate collapsing from ~99% to ~2-3% in the same 6-minute bucket containing 12:14-12:20Z.

events.statement: Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in 10:00-13:00Z: settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510), 'Batch settlement report export', deployed 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z by ci-bot, change 'new CSV exporter', status live with rolled_back_at null.

Exactly one config change occurred across all services in 10:00-13:00Z: payment-service key bank.api.timeout_ms changed 3000 -> 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z (author p.nair, 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory').
payment-service itself had zero deployments in 08:00-14:00Z (count 0), and settlement-service had zero config changes in the same window (count 0).

payment-service's dependency graph: edges payment-service -> ledger-db (db), payment-service -> bank-partner-api (external), payment-service -> kafka (queue-produce), and api-gateway -> payment-service (http). ledger-db and kafka are marked shared:true; bank-partner-api has has_telemetry:false.

ledger-db is shared by four services — order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all hold db edges into it — so the settlement-service deployment lands on a datastore that payment-service also writes to.

Historical precedent matching the 'users report failures / downstream degradation' pattern: HIST-111 (2025-05-22) 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db', services ledger-db + settlement-service, root_cause 'New report query without index did sequential scans', category bad_deployment. Also relevant: HIST-105 payment failures from bank partner API 5xx (dependency_failure). These are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

events.answer: In 2026-04-02T10:00-13:00Z exactly two changes occurred across all services: a payment-service config change raising the bank API timeout (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000, 11:20Z), and a settlement-service deployment (dep-5510, v1.9.0 "Batch settlement report export", 10:30Z, still live, not rolled back). payment-service has no deployments in that window. payment-service depends on the shared ledger-db and kafka, and settlement-service also writes to the same shared ledger-db — matching the pattern of historical incident HIST-111, where a settlement reporting job degraded ledger-db. Payment-service's error-rate panel staying green is consistent with a downstream/shared-resource degradation that surfaces to users without raising payment-service's own HTTP error rate.

events.statement: The cert-watcher WARN log predates the failure and warns of the exact expiry: 'cert-watcher: client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)' at 2026-04-02T11:50:26Z, 25 minutes before expiry at 12:15:00Z. This timing is independent of either candidate change.

ledger-db cpu_pct is flat across the entire 11:30-13:00Z window (mean 29.98%, min 27.41, max 32.82, 0 missing points) with no rise in the 12:15Z bucket (avg 29.17) where payment failures begin — no shared-datastore resource spike aligning with onset.

ledger-db slow_queries_per_min rises to 9.02 avg / 9.63 max in the 12:00Z bucket and 4.25 in 11:55Z, but is back to baseline by the 12:10Z bucket (0.91) and stays ~1.0 through 12:15Z (1.11) and 12:20Z (0.75) — the blip is ~15-20 min BEFORE the 12:15Z payment onset, not coincident with it.

ledger-db replication_lag_ms (mean 39.86, min 35.27, max 44.34) and connections_active (mean 62.1, min 55.91, max 69.24) are stable across 11:30-13:00Z with no anomaly in the 12:15Z bucket. Also, ledger-db has NO p99-latency metric ('service ledger-db has no metric latency_p99_ms'; available: connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min).

settlement-service emitted ZERO ERROR logs in 10:30-12:30Z (total_matched 0), so the dep-5510 CSV-exporter deployment shows no error signature around the payment onset. No ledger-db logs either (total_matched 0).

Across the onset window, the 80+ payment-service errors are 100% TLS client-cert expiry against bank-partner-api ('remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'), and there is no evidence tying either the dep-5510 deploy (10:30Z) or the bank.api.timeout_ms change (11:20Z) to the cert expiry or to a downstream resource/latency trend at 12:14-12:15Z. The only downstream dependency showing an anomaly is bank-partner-api, whose rejection (via expired client cert) is observed entirely within payment-service logs/metrics.

bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry:false — no metrics or logs of its own; it can only be observed through payment-service.
Did not verify whether the bank.api.timeout_ms change (11:20Z) or dep-5510 altered any cert-rotation/renewal path; no config/service inventory for cert-watcher was retrieved.

events.answer: Neither candidate change correlates with the failure onset. The only change touching payment-service is the bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 config (11:20Z), which cannot expire a TLS certificate, and the settlement-service dep-5510 deploy (10:30Z) touches shared ledger-db — but ledger-db shows no resource/latency/error trend at the 12:15Z onset (cpu flat ~30%, replication_lag ~40ms, connections ~62, slow_queries back to baseline by 12:10Z) and settlement-service emits no errors in 10:30-12:30Z. The failure is a TLS client-certificate expiry (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) surfaced by payment-service when calling the downstream bank-partner-api, whose mTLS handshake rejects it; the anomalies are confined to payment-service's outbound bank calls, not to a shared/downstream datastore. Most likely trigger = certificate expiry on payment-service's bank client cert, not a deploy/config change.

Bank/acquirer side (external) failure causing the rejections

events.summary: H1 is well supported and the alternatives are affirmatively contradicted, not merely dismissed. Grounding: the causal chain's key links are verified observations — a hard, schedulable cert property (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, F2), an independent pre-onset log predicting the exact expiry 25 min earlier (F14, cert-watcher 11:50:26Z), the first TLS alert-45 at 12:15:27Z and continuation to 13:58:39Z (F1/F2), 100% of errors being that single signature (F19), and the green-panel mechanism explained by business-level PENDING_RETRY instead of HTTP 5xx (F7, corroborated by flat error_rate 0.16-0.26% with request_rate unchanged, F5). Temporal order is the strongest part: the cause is a fixed timestamp that precedes onset by ~27 seconds, and the independent F14 log establishes the timeline without reference to either candidate change. Scope: symptoms are confined to the single anomalous dependency path bank-partner-api (F6/F11/F19); all other neighbors (ledger-db, kafka) are flat (F15-F17). Alternatives were tested, not assumed away: H3 was killed by directly contradicting telemetry (flat ledger-db cpu/lag/connections F15/F17, slow-query blip peaking 12:00Z and baseline by 12:10Z i.e. BEFORE onset F16, zero settlement-service errors F18, ~105-min quiet gap), and H2 has no mechanism (a timeout change cannot emit a client-cert alert 45). Data-quality caveats exist but do not affect ranking: the metric onset is bucket-bounded (12:14-12:20Z) while logs pin 12:15:27Z; ledger-db lacks a p99 metric and emits no logs, so it is excluded mainly by the flat cpu/lag/connections plus the pre-onset slow-query blip rather than by a negative latency measurement. The one genuine unverified link — F2's 'our client cert' wording is self-incriminating and F6/F11 show the bank side has no telemetry, so the bank side cannot be independently confirmed — is an assumption that is internally corroborated (independent F14 prediction of the same notAfter) and does not create a rival hypothesis with evidence behind it. No open question identified by the team could plausibly reorder the ranking; they are either already established (single-route scoping, exact onset within 27s) or unobtainable (bank-side telemetry, permanently absent). Further rounds would spend outage minutes for no ranking-changing information.

events.why: top hypothesis is above threshold and clearly ahead

tasks.objective: Determine whether the reported payment failures are real and when they started. Around 2026-04-02T12:17-12:32Z, look beyond HTTP error-rate: check payment-service request rate, latency, business-level failure signals (declined/failed transfer counts, status fields in logs, 200-with-error-body patterns), logs for error signatures mentioning bank/acquirer/transfer/decline/timeout, and any affected dependency traces. Report onset time, exact error signatures, and which services/endpoints actually show anomalies vs. the green error-rate panel.
tasks.answer: The payment failures are real and start at ~2026-04-02T12:15Z. The HTTP error-rate panel is green by design flaw: the failures never reach an HTTP 5xx because payment-service returns a success-style response while marking transfers PENDING_RETRY after the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api is rejected. The exact signature is an expired client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, "tls: expired certificate (alert 45)"), with bank_api_error_rate jumping from 0.2% to 100% and payment_success_rate collapsing from ~99% to ~2-3% in the same 6-minute bucket containing 12:14-12:20Z.

tasks.objective: Identify what changed across ALL services (not just payment-service) in the window 2026-04-02T10:00Z-13:00Z: list deployments and config changes, especially to payment-service's dependencies (bank/acquirer gateway, transfer/ledger workers, queues, shared infrastructure). Also map payment-service's dependency graph and shared components, and search historical incidents for the same 'users report failures but error rate green' pattern with its known root cause.
tasks.answer: In 2026-04-02T10:00-13:00Z exactly two changes occurred across all services: a payment-service config change raising the bank API timeout (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000, 11:20Z), and a settlement-service deployment (dep-5510, v1.9.0 "Batch settlement report export", 10:30Z, still live, not rolled back). payment-service has no deployments in that window. payment-service depends on the shared ledger-db and kafka, and settlement-service also writes to the same shared ledger-db — matching the pattern of historical incident HIST-111, where a settlement reporting job degraded ledger-db. Payment-service's error-rate panel staying green is consistent with a downstream/shared-resource degradation that surfaces to users without raising payment-service's own HTTP error rate.

tasks.objective: Correlate the changes found in task b against the symptom onset found in task a. For each candidate change (deploy/config) in the onset window, check whether the downstream dependency it touched shows a matching resource/error/latency trend in the same minutes. Conclude which specific change, if any, is the most likely trigger and whether the failure is in payment-service itself or a downstream dependency.
tasks.answer: Neither candidate change correlates with the failure onset. The only change touching payment-service is the bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 config (11:20Z), which cannot expire a TLS certificate, and the settlement-service dep-5510 deploy (10:30Z) touches shared ledger-db — but ledger-db shows no resource/latency/error trend at the 12:15Z onset (cpu flat ~30%, replication_lag ~40ms, connections ~62, slow_queries back to baseline by 12:10Z) and settlement-service emits no errors in 10:30-12:30Z. The failure is a TLS client-certificate expiry (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) surfaced by payment-service when calling the downstream bank-partner-api, whose mTLS handshake rejects it; the anomalies are confined to payment-service's outbound bank calls, not to a shared/downstream datastore. Most likely trigger = certificate expiry on payment-service's bank client cert, not a deploy/config change.

critiques.summary: H1 is well supported and the alternatives are affirmatively contradicted, not merely dismissed. Grounding: the causal chain's key links are verified observations — a hard, schedulable cert property (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, F2), an independent pre-onset log predicting the exact expiry 25 min earlier (F14, cert-watcher 11:50:26Z), the first TLS alert-45 at 12:15:27Z and continuation to 13:58:39Z (F1/F2), 100% of errors being that single signature (F19), and the green-panel mechanism explained by business-level PENDING_RETRY instead of HTTP 5xx (F7, corroborated by flat error_rate 0.16-0.26% with request_rate unchanged, F5). Temporal order is the strongest part: the cause is a fixed timestamp that precedes onset by ~27 seconds, and the independent F14 log establishes the timeline without reference to either candidate change. Scope: symptoms are confined to the single anomalous dependency path bank-partner-api (F6/F11/F19); all other neighbors (ledger-db, kafka) are flat (F15-F17). Alternatives were tested, not assumed away: H3 was killed by directly contradicting telemetry (flat ledger-db cpu/lag/connections F15/F17, slow-query blip peaking 12:00Z and baseline by 12:10Z i.e. BEFORE onset F16, zero settlement-service errors F18, ~105-min quiet gap), and H2 has no mechanism (a timeout change cannot emit a client-cert alert 45). Data-quality caveats exist but do not affect ranking: the metric onset is bucket-bounded (12:14-12:20Z) while logs pin 12:15:27Z; ledger-db lacks a p99 metric and emits no logs, so it is excluded mainly by the flat cpu/lag/connections plus the pre-onset slow-query blip rather than by a negative latency measurement. The one genuine unverified link — F2's 'our client cert' wording is self-incriminating and F6/F11 show the bank side has no telemetry, so the bank side cannot be independently confirmed — is an assumption that is internally corroborated (independent F14 prediction of the same notAfter) and does not create a rival hypothesis with evidence behind it. No open question identified by the team could plausibly reorder the ranking; they are either already established (single-route scoping, exact onset within 27s) or unobtainable (bank-side telemetry, permanently absent). Further rounds would spend outage minutes for no ranking-changing information.

challenges.issue: The party enforcing and reporting the cert rejection is the bank gateway, which has has_telemetry:false (F6/F11); the alert-45 text and the 'our client cert' attribution rest entirely on the caller's view and cannot be independently confirmed from the bank side. This is correctly listed as an assumption and is mitigated by F14 independently naming the same notAfter 25 min earlier, so it does not block the conclusion.

Onset is established at two granularities: logs pin 12:15:27Z but the metric bucket (360s) only bounds it to 12:14-12:20Z. The cause (notAfter=12:15:00Z) nonetheless precedes the tightest observed onset by 27s, so temporal order is sound; the bucket granularity is a precision caveat, not a gap.

ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms and emits no logs, so its exclusion rests on flat cpu_pct/replication_lag_ms/connections_active (F15/F17) plus a slow-query blip that resolves BEFORE onset (F16), rather than a direct latency/error negative. This is sufficient because the same queries also fail to show any 12:15Z-aligned anomaly, and the actual failure signature is a TLS cert alert unrelated to datastore latency (F19).

Rejected partly on mechanism grounds (timeout change cannot expire a cert) which is a valid a-priori argument, but it is also rejected on evidence: failures carry a fixed notAfter independent of the 11:20Z change and the change precedes onset by ~55 min with no alignment (F2/F14/F19).
